A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Decoding Game research. Their main text, equations, tables, Figure 1, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison despite restructuring and added evaluations.

before.justification: Section 5 and Table 1 report original GPT-2 text-generation evaluations. Appendix B includes parameter sensitivity results and a truncation case study.

after.justification: Section 5 reports original evaluations across GPT-2, GPT-J-6B, and Llama-2-7B with several decoding methods. Appendix B provides additional parameter sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same epsilon-dependent truncation, temperature-dependent weighting, normalization, and token sampling. Threshold notation changes, but the procedure does not; the adaptive-epsilon discussion explains a connection to Nucleus sampling.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate open-ended generation on WebText and retain the one-token versus 35-token context illustration. The added language models change experimental configurations, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands comparisons from Nucleus, Greedy, and Pure sampling to also include Contrastive search, Typical sampling, and Basis-Aware sampling (BA-η). These additions appear in the corresponding GPT-2 comparisons as well as the new model evaluations.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands substantially beyond four GPT-2 sizes to GPT-J-6B and Llama-2-7B. The existing protocol remains: 5,000 WebText articles, 35-token prompts, maximum 256-token generations, the same three metrics, and MAUVE-based hyperparameter selection.

E4.justification: New Table 3 extends the existing epsilon/temperature sensitivity analysis to GPT-J-6B and Llama-2-7B. The GPT-2 sweeps in Table 2 and the truncation case study in Figure 1 are retained; no substantially different analytical question is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional results retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing GPT-2 results are retained apart from equivalent rounding, while Tables 1 and 3 add substantial comparison and sensitivity results. Newly reported GPT-J-6B MAUVE is 0.833 for Game versus 0.826 for BA-η; on Llama-2-7B, Game scores 0.858 versus BA-η's 0.890. These are added findings under new model settings.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 refines no foresight through agreement of conditional distributions along a history, replacing the earlier formulation using past conditional maps. Section 4.2 adds a cumulative-probability bound and a large-I approximation for the entropy-offset term. The principal minimax theorems and Appendix A proof strategies remain.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows the criticism of deterministic likelihood-maximizing decoding to open-ended generation and acknowledges its success on closed-ended tasks. The central claims concerning minimax decoding, implicit regularization, first-order truncation-normalization optimality, and temperature generalization are retained.

C2.justification: v2 explains that extending the analysis beyond TV distance, such as to KL divergence, requires different techniques. It also clarifies that recovering Nucleus sampling requires distribution-dependent adaptive epsilon and adds a computational-cost qualification concerning BA-η.

D1.justification: Table 1 documents selected hyperparameters for the added comparators: Contrastive alpha 0.6, Typical p 0.9, and BA-η eta 0.0001. Tables 1 and 3 also specify Game sampling settings for the added models. There is no corresponding expansion of hardware, runtime, or project-code documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Shi et al. (2024), Wiher et al. (2022), Su et al. (2022), and sources for the evaluated models. Section 2.3 adds ridge/lasso examples of robustness–regularization equivalence. The existing related-work framework and principal novelty positioning remain.

P1.justification: Section 3 is substantially reorganized, introducing the one-step game before the multi-step reduction and replacing the standalone probability-structure subsection. Appendix A.2 receives extensive expository rewriting with labeled ordering and KKT stages, alongside expanded introductory explanations and theoretical remarks.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains comparator rows and two model panels, and Appendix B adds Table 3. These extend the existing panel-based table design. Figure 1's two plots are unchanged, while retained material is reflowed and resized.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline and model evaluations make the empirical support more informative, including evidence that BA-η outperforms Game on Llama-2. The clearer formulation and qualification to open-ended tasks also help. Gains remain limited by point-estimate-only reporting and a general temperature discussion that does not address the increasing repetition at higher temperatures in the new Llama-2 results.
